claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
The single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline has a coercive field of 100 Oe.
Aging at 500°C for 10 hours will form coherent L1₂ precipitates in FeCoNi.
The proposed precipitates have the Ni₃Fe composition and L1₂ structure.
The L1₂ precipitates will be coherent with the fcc matrix.
Water quenching after aging will preserve the proposed precipitate-containing microstructure at room temperature.
Coherent L1₂ precipitates will pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning will increase the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Increasing the energy required for domain-wall motion will increase the coercive field.
The intervention will increase coercivity by at least 50% relative to the stated baseline.
The coercive field will increase from 100 Oe to at least 150 Oe.
Precipitate size and distribution may affect domain-wall-pinning efficiency and coercivity.
A matched alloy without the aging-induced secondary phase will serve as the experimental control.
Coercivity, saturation magnetization, and hysteresis-loop shape will be measured.

contradictions.description: The prediction is satisfied at 150 Oe because it states 'at least 150 Oe,' whereas the falsification rule requires an increase strictly greater than 150 Oe. Thus, an observed value of exactly 150 Oe is both within the predicted outcome and falsifying under the stated rule.
